- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean or 1–2 points.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% or 1–2 points.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon; reduce first 5–7 forecast points by 1–3% to align with true drop-offs.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or use 20-day moving average as ceiling.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85), model tends to lag; add 1–2 points to forecast to catch reversal.
- When sentiment is flat (0.0) and history shows volatility, model underreacts; increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 per day to reflect latent momentum.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >3% over 3–5 days, model is biased low; apply upward correction proportional to sentiment strength (e.g., 0.2×sentiment×10 for 10-day horizon).
